systemicFindings: The round-three repair materially fixed nine of the fifteen rejected entries.

Six entries still confuse the person mentioned or performing an action with the utterer of the headword-bearing words. Formal exact-KWIC and attribution-shape gates do not detect this semantic substitution.
The 35 prior KEEP entries remain byte-identical. No entry was edited, promoted, merged, or exposed to the site by this review.

rows.finding: KEEP — The two round-two defects are corrected: Tiantai Deshao owns the continuous address and Mahakasyapa owns his explicit question. Fresh rereading found no residual contamination, duplicate pseudo-depth, sense, or prose defect.

REVISE — O7 and O8 now substitute Manjusri, the person mentioned inside the passages, for the utterer. O8 is in Dahui Zonggao’s continuous public discourse: Dahui says that a visitor had just asked about Manjusri ordering Sudhana to gather medicine, then comments on Manjusri. Manjusri does not utter the headword there. O7 is likewise a headword mention inside a recorded master’s exposition, not a Manjusri turn. The duplicate Source-Mirror windows were repaired, but exact-turn attribution remains wrong.

REVISE — The Shoushan canonical-name defect is fixed, but action narration is still stored as master utterance. O2 says the master pointed at the jars with a staff and then spoke; the narrator, not Baizhang, utters the headword. O3, O4, and O10 likewise place the headword in narration of a master’s staff action before or outside quoted speech. The acting master belongs in ContextMasters, while MasterName must remain null unless he utters the headword-bearing words.

KEEP — Yongming Yanshou and Xinghua Shaoqing are now resolved from their continuous discourses, and the paired Nanquan witnesses are explicitly treated as parallel transmission rather than independent semantic depth. All six cases remain eligible and coherent.

REVISE — Canonical identities are repaired, but the exact-headword-turn rule is still violated. O1 is narrator-owned event framing (“on opening-furnace day … mounted the seat, saying”), O3 narrates Fayan mounting the seat before a monk asks, and O6 is the heading/event frame “Secretary Chuan invited [him] to mount the seat” before Huqiu’s address. These masters perform or follow the action; they do not utter the headword-bearing narration.

REVISE — Duplicate windows were removed and Nengren Jian is restored, but subject/utterer substitution remains. O6 embeds narration that Dongshan called an attendant inside a later master’s citation; Dongshan is the described actor, not the utterer of 侍者. O10 similarly says Qinshan instructed an attendant to ask: the attendant later asks other words but does not utter the headword. These need narrator/quoter ownership with the named figures in context roles.
